method: Slice fub: former CEOs and other named executive officers of US-listed companies whose shareholders lost heavily during their tenure, then appointed non-employee directors of a different US-listed company. Candidates came from (a) known CEO departures 2014-2024, (b) the CEO-change market screen, and (c) EDGAR full-text searches of Form 3 filings by name after each departure, which list new issuers whose boards the person joined. Each candidate was then checked in filings only. The A test uses a tabulated cumulative-return table in A's own 10-K (or the proxy pay-versus-performance table where the 10-K graph is image-only). The table must have its base date and end point inside the person's tenure in the role, and show a loss of at least 40% or a shortfall of at least 50 points against an index or peer group in the same table. The window is the table with the earliest in-tenure base, read to its latest in-tenure point. A case is rejected if any other in-tenure window in A's own filings at least as long (earlier or later) shows the stock ahead of its comparison; later tables checked are cited in notes. For a CEO the test uses the CEO tenure; earlier roles are noted but not tested. A's float was at least about $500M. The B seat had to begin after the window's end and within 3 years of leaving A; seats begun during the window are rejected. B pay is the 'Total' column of B's proxy Director Compensation table for every fiscal year through the latest 2026 proxy; partial first years are included as reported. Exit pay is recorded only where a filing quantifies it; golden-parachute figures are labeled as estimates. Quotes are verbatim from bt.text.document_text output (whitespace normalized).
